t: Webb Reveals New Details in Supernova Remnant

img.cap: A colorful, roughly circular supernova remnant, named Cassiopeia A, set on the black background of space. There are many orange and green filaments with smoke-like consistencies that extend from the center toward the edges of the frame. The green filaments loosely weave throughout the remnant and compose much of the edge of the remnant, while, between the center and the edges, the orange filaments are more densely packed into an irregular ring-like shape. Toward the top right and bottom left of the dense, orange filaments, there are light blue pockets of gas and dust.

p: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A. The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star.NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A (Cas A) in this high-resolution, mid-infrared image released on Nov. 23, 2026. Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. The Webb data supports a scenario in which the interior of the star underwent a dramatic change, possibly just hours before its demise.
